title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centers: unified management of Teams apps and agents across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing prerequisites and documented controls are supported by Microsoft's sources. Two minor corrections remain: complete the availability-setting route and remove the setup-policy inventory instruction that has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Administrators can manage cross-application Teams apps and agents from either admin centre across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.claim: The roadmap states that previously Integrated Apps changes affected these apps only in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: Before this update, changes made through the Integrated Apps section in the Microsoft 365 admin center would only affect these apps on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App

claims.claim: The roadmap states that previously Teams admin center changes affected only Teams.
claims.quote: similarly, changes made in the Teams admin center would exclusively affect Teams.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Org-wide setting changes are automatically synchronised in both directions after tenant unification.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: App status changes, including allow or block, are synchronised between admin centres after unification.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Availability and user-assignment changes in one centre reach the other after unification.
claims.quote: Ensures consistent and synchronized agent and app behavior across platforms, as changes to app availability settings in one admin center are automatically synced with the other

claims.claim: The cross-application guide still describes separate Teams and MAC settings, unlike the unification guide's post-unification synchronisation.
claims.quote: Any changes made on the integrated apps portal on the Microsoft 365 admin center only impact whether and how a cross application app is surfaced on Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application. To manage how these apps show up on Teams, use the Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The default is on: never-modified tenants are unified automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: Tenants that modified settings can choose unification through Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: If your tenant has custom app changes but no differences in app availability: 1. Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. 2. Select Move to unified app management.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The alignment wizard compares differing settings and lets administrators choose which centre's settings to apply.
claims.quote: Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the Apply settings from drop-down list and select Apply settings.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final unification changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Any Teams or Global admin can prepare updates up to Review summary.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.claim: MC796790 includes a text update dated 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Phase 1, for never-modified tenants, began rolling out at the end of September 2025.
claims.quote: App and agent availability unification (Section A): Rollout began in late September 2025.

claims.claim: Phase 2 for modified tenants is fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Phase 2 applies no org-wide or app-level setting changes without administrator action.
claims.quote: Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Autonomy & actions; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Phase 3 will automatically unify availability for tenants that have not acted.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft will announce Phase 3's timeline at least 60 days before that phase begins.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The supplied notice has not announced a Phase 3 start date.
claims.quote: Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future) ... We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.claim: Unified app and agent installation management is generally available.
claims.quote: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Installation unification applies to tenants whose app and agent availability is unified.
claims.quote: Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible.

claims.claim: Supported installations are synchronised across the centres within 24 to 48 hours of availability unification.
claims.quote: app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says app installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.
claims.quote: Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Installations previously made through Teams app setup policies are not unified by this change.
claims.quote: Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.claim: MC796790 names roadmap items 393931, 485712 and 503105.
claims.quote: This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping the two centres' settings synchronised until tenant unification to prevent disruption.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized. This measure prevents unexpected disruptions or issues with agent and app functionality.

claims.claim: Microsoft's unification pages describe no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management data approval. Read microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac, manage-apps, apps-in-teams and MC796790; unification changes availability, status, org-wide settings and installations, with no new data-access mechanism described.

claims.claim: The unification page describes no approval step for each synchronised change.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management data approval. Read microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac and manage-apps; synchronisation is automatic after unification, and the documented consent is for entering the unified state, not for each subsequent change.

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: App availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to reach the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.claim: The entitlement model is included within the licences that the administered product already requires.
claims.quote: The following licensing options include agents that can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center: ... Microsoft 365 plans ... Microsoft Copilot ... Microsoft Agent 365

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agent management requires the organisation's required subscription and licences for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot or Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: Your organization has the required subscription and licenses for either Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, or Microsoft Agent 365.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users who create, publish or use agents need appropriate assigned licences.
claims.quote: Users at your organization that create, publish, or use agents have the appropriate licenses assigned.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate licence for unification itself is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management licensing subscription price meter Microsoft Teams admin center; unified app management license price. Read uam-tac-mac, agent-365-overview, cross-application app guide, purchase-third-party-apps and MC796790; no unification-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate meter for unification itself is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management licensing subscription price meter Microsoft Teams admin center; unified app management license price. Read uam-tac-mac, agent-365-overview, cross-application app guide, purchase-third-party-apps and MC796790; no unification meter.

claims.claim: Licences or fees for individual third-party apps are separate publisher offerings.
claims.quote: Developers can create SaaS offers associated with their Teams apps. These offers are published through Partner Center and are available for organizations to purchase through AppSource and the Microsoft Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Teams Administrator as the role for using the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Developers can enhance Teams apps to work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App.
claims.quote: App developers can enhance their Microsoft Teams apps to work in Outlook and in Microsoft 365 App (formerly known as Office.com).

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management starts tenant unification.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Move to unified app management. The Align org-wide app settings page appears.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls prose; Open questions
claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation is documented for moving the tenant to unified management or checking its unification state.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management tenant migration unification state PowerShell MicrosoftTeams Graph API; MicrosoftTeams unified app management migration PowerShell cmdlet. Read uam-tac-mac, app-centric-management and Update-M365TeamsApp; no tenant-unification operation.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the individual app or agent's status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams module documents Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -IsBlocked $true as an app-state operation.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The printed Teams app availability route reaches Edit availability through Users and groups and Availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. ... select Availability. ... Select Edit availability. ... Select the required option from Available to menu.
claims.fix: Complete controls[2].ui.path and its rendered row as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to > Specific users or groups'. This is the specific-user/group option documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group IDs> adds group app-availability assignments.
claims.quote: -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add ... -Groups 37da2d58-fc14-453e-9a14-5065ebd63a1d ... updates availability setting for the app to include 2 users and 5 groups.

claims.claim: The app-centric page says availability cannot be updated in bulk in TAC but can be through PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Custom apps > Let users install and use available apps by default reaches the Custom apps switch.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp -isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled $True enables the org-wide Custom apps switch.
claims.quote: There is a switch for managing Custom Apps in the Org-wide App Settings page of Teams Admin Center. The command can set the value of this switch. If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled.

claims.where: controls[3].governs and note; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The custom-app cmdlet covers uploading and making custom apps available, not the other app-type switches.
claims.quote: The value to Custom Apps Setting. If the value is true, the custom apps can be uploaded as app packages and available in the organization's app store, vice versa.

claims.claim: MAC > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install sets availability.
claims.quote: Select Settings, then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... select the app ... select the Users tab ... Specific users/group in the organization can install

claims.claim: No separate MAC-side API operation for this Integrated apps availability control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Integrated apps availability specific users groups Graph API PowerShell; Integrated apps availability Graph API; Microsoft 365 admin center integrated app availability automation API users groups. Read cross-application guide and Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.claim: The cited cmdlet references do not describe how each call appears in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Integrated apps availability specific users groups Graph API PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp unified. Read Update-M365TeamsApp and Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp; neither specifies the MAC presentation of its calls.

claims.claim: Administrators can export the app catalogue from TAC's Manage apps page to review status and availability.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: The unification wizard has Align org-wide app settings and Align app-level settings and supports bulk resolution for selected apps.
claims.quote: Bulk app resolution: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the Apply settings from drop-down list.

claims.where: Governance controls prose; Open questions: roles
claims.claim: The cited cross-application guide restricts its Integrated apps controls to Global Admins.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.

claims.claim: The cited cross-application guide does not explain the interaction of its Global Admin restriction with the Teams Administrator role after unification.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 admin center integrated app availability automation API users groups. Read teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365 and uam-tac-mac; the cross-application guide states Global Admins only but does not discuss the post-unification Teams Administrator interaction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, setup-policy installation inventory
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to take stock of appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'List apps that users received through Teams app setup policies'. Controls: tenant unification, app blocking, app availability, Custom apps and MAC availability; no setup-policy installation-assignment row.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'List apps that users received through Teams app setup policies'. Keep the supported setup-policy installation limitation in Risk assessment.
